name: ruan
title: Ruan (zhongruan)
builder: _plucked(ring_seconds=1.8, low_pass=3500.0, slope=6.0, position=0.15, pick=0.05). From the source: four single steel strings on a round wooden body, played with a plectrum, a mellow tone. Sound design: every number
notes: Ruan page: 'It is a lute with a fretted neck, a circular body, and four strings. Its four strings were formerly made of silk but since the 20th century they have been made of steel (flatwound for the lower strings).'; 'Mainstream ruan players use plectrums'; 'Plectrums produce a louder and more clear tone'; 'The instrument produces a mellow tone.' Range for the tenor size, the one the page says is in common use ('In Chinese orchestras, only the zhongruan and daruan are commonly used'): 'tenor: zhongruan (中阮, lit. "medium ruan"; tuning: G2-D3-G3-D4)'; 'The modern ruan has 24 frets with 12 semitones on each string, which has greatly expanded its range from a previous 13 frets.' Derivation: lowest G2; highest D4 + 24 frets = D6. Judgment call: I read "24 frets with 12 semitones on each string" as 24 chromatic frets (each fret a semitone), so the top is the highest open string plus 24 semitones. Told apart (rule 7) from acoustic guitar (steel, pick, but bright: low pass 6500 Hz, ring 3.0 s) by the sourced mellow tone of its small round body, from jazz guitar (mellow, but fingered: no pick) by the plectrum, and from pipa and the SHORT_LUTE shapes (bright, ringing 0.9 s) by the mellow tone. hs 321.3: a fretted neck (no number on the page)
